title: Platform systems & services: Ops playbook, runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical ops playbook for the Platform (systems & services) team. It combines the team wiki, runbooks for common incidents, dashboard and alert ownership, retrospective summaries, and a near-term roadmap. The intended audience is Platform engineers, SREs, and on-call engineers who need a single reference for operating Redwood’s platform services.

Scope
- Services covered: control-plane APIs, routing/gateway, scheduler, autoscaler, KV cache service, model-routing service, metrics & tracing pipelines, and the dashboards/alerting stack.
- Excluded: customer on-prem packages (see eng-private-deployments), model training jobs.

Key contacts and ownership
- Platform Lead: Jordan Kim (platform-systems)
- On-call rotation owner: Priya Rao
- Observability owner: Liam Chen
- Pager escalation: Platform oncall -> Platform+Infra -> Eng-SRE -> CTO on-call

SLOs and reliability targets
- Control-plane API availability: 99.95% monthly (target)
- Median request latency (control-plane): < 40 ms
- Model-routing 95th p50 token latency: < 250 ms for tier=standard models
- Metrics ingestion: 99% of metrics within 60s of event time

Dashboards and alerts (owner annotations)
- Dashboards
  - Platform Overview (owner: Liam Chen): traffic, error rate, top-latency paths, capacity headroom.
  - Autoscaler Health (owner: Jordan Kim): pending pods, scale events, backoff counts.
  - Model Routing & Cache (owner: Platform SRE): KV cache hit rate, model variant fallbacks, per-model latency heatmap.
  - Ingest & Pipeline (owner: Observability): metric lag, dropped samples, promoter success rate.

- Key alerts (PagerDuty -> platform_oncall)
  - control_plane_5xx_rate > 5% for 5m -> P1
  - control_plane_latency_p95 > 500ms for 10m -> P1
  - metrics_pipeline_lag > 120s for 10m -> P2
  - autoscaler_backoff_count > 5 in 15m -> P2
  - kv_cache_hit_rate < 60% and increased downstream latency -> P2
  - token_queue_length > 1000 for 5m (inference queue) -> P1

Alert runbook templates
- For each P1/P2 alert create a ticket and follow the corresponding runbook below. Include alert id, time, and top-line impact in the ticket description.

Runbooks (short versions)
1) Control-plane high 5xx rate (P1)
1. Acknowledge pager and post to #platform-incident with alert details.
2. Check Platform Overview dashboard for spikes by endpoint and deployment versions.
3. Run quick health checks:
   - curl -s -D - https://control-plane.internal/ping | head -n 20
   - kubectl get pods -n control-plane -o wide | egrep "CrashLoop|OOM|Error"
4. If a recent rollout is present, roll back using the deployment tag and trigger canary rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane -n control-plane --to-revision=<prev>.
5. If downstream dependency (auth, db) failing: check dependency runbooks (DB outage, Auth degraded).
6. Create incident ticket, capture SLO impact, assign owner for postmortem.

2) Inference token queue spike / model routing degradation (P1)
1. Check Model Routing & Cache dashboard: per-model queue length and worker utilization.
2. Identify whether the spike is traffic-driven or worker degradation (GPU/OOM) using:
   - sh prometheus-query.sh "sum(token_queue_length) by (model)"
   - kubectl top pods -n inference | sort -k3 -nr | head
3. If workers are saturated: increase worker pool via autoscaler override (only for short-term): kubectl scale deployment/inference-worker --replicas=<N> -n inference (follow burst policy in infra-standards).
4. If memory OOM observed: capture pod logs (kubectl logs <pod>) and mark image as suspect; scale down and failover to a cheaper model-variant if configured.
5. If KV cache miss storm: identify cache TTL/regeneration and consider temporary cache warming (replay hot prefixes).
6. Engage ML infra owner and open incident ticket.

3) Metrics ingestion lag or pipeline failure (P2)
1. Validate Prometheus pushgateway and Kafka topic status: kafka-topics.sh --describe --zookeeper zk:2181 --topic metrics_ingest
2. Check Prometheus remote_write errors and connector logs.
3. Restart connector for the affected shard: systemctl restart metrics-connector@shard-<id>.service (or kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-connector -n observability).
4. If persistent: open observability incident and rehydrate metrics from raw logs for critical dashboards.

Operational procedures and checklists
- Daily (oncall morning): review Platform Overview dashboard, check for any unresolved alerts, verify autoscaler headroom > 20% total capacity, verify SLO dashboard shows 0 active SLO breaches.
- Weekly: run chaos-lite tests in staging (simulated worker OOM, network partition) and validate alert firing and runbook effectiveness.
- Monthly: capacity planning sync with eng-infra, review reserved capacity, and update model-routing cost forecast.

CI/CD and safe rollout guidance
- All control-plane changes must pass: unit tests, integration tests, contract tests, and a 10% canary for 30 minutes with rollback on 5xx spike > 1% above baseline.
- Commands:
  - Create canary: kubectl rollout restart deployment/control-plane -n control-plane --record
  - Monitor: grafana dashboard url: https://grafana.internal/d/PLATFORM_OVERVIEW

Retrospective notes (Q4 2026)
- Incident: model-routing regression on 2026-11-09 caused 30m of elevated latency for tier-standard models. Root cause: regression in cache key serialization introduced by model-routing v2.1.2.
- Actions taken: immediate rollback to v2.1.1, added serialization unit tests, added canary for model-routing changes.
- Outcome: reduced recurrence risk; action items completed and tracked in ticket PLAT-2026-349.

Roadmap (next 90 days)
- Short-term (Q1 2027):
  - Automate cache warming for hot prefixes (owner: Platform SRE)
  - Add end-to-end synthetic load tests for common inference paths (owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime)
  - Dashboard refresh: combine per-model latency heatmap with cost-per-token (owner: Observability)
- Mid-term (Q2 2027 planning):
  - Autoscaler improvements: predictive scaling based on traffic forecasts
  - Platform runbook automation: one-click remediation playbooks in Console

Post-incident review and blameless retros
- All P1 incidents must have a postmortem within 7 days, with a designated action owner and ETA. Templates: include timeline, detection, mitigation, root cause, and action list. Link postmortems to the related Jira tickets and to the incident channel thread.

Contributing and links
- To update runbooks or dashboards: submit a PR to docs/confluence (follow the Confluence sync process). For runbook changes that affect oncall procedure, add reviewers: oncall-owner and observability owner.
- Useful links:
  - Platform runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-runbook-roadmap-2026.json
  - On-call schedule: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks
  - Infra standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/infra-standards

Appendix: Quick reference commands
- kubectl get pods -n <ns> -o wide
- kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous
- kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <ns> --to-revision=<rev>
- prometheus-query.sh "sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) by (job)"

Change history
- 2025-11-12: created by Jordan Kim.
- 2026-02-15: updated dashboards and added Q4 2026 retrospective notes.
